progressNotes.summary: Fixed 5 exit-path defects (b38afcd) and made the curriculum engine report and fill executable-capability gaps (d2d6608). 365 passed, audit 91/91. Key findings: the lot ledger was per-strategy so no strategy could ever close another's lot (all 4 historical SELLs closed nothing); the 24h PnL window could not match June lots; verified PnL was silently dropped before the lifecycle layer saw it; max_position_value truncated exits; guardian min_confidence=0.5 was admission-blind. Live: June lots now reconstruct as {tiny-fixed-size-001:13, fixed-size-buy-001:6, trend-follow-buy-001:4}, capability coverage correctly reports SELL uncovered at the real 767.25, and the daemon admitted trend-follow-buy-002 at 17:43.
progressNotes.next: Keep the live loop running until a SELL strategy is admitted and selected, then let a real order fill so a closed lot and per-strategy PnL form naturally. No rigging: do not alter risk limits, prompts to force a trade, or the market. Restore the curriculum interval to the shipped default once observed.

Goal substantially achieved and the system now runs end to end. 384 tests pass, audit 91/91, doctor 0 failures. The self-evolution loop is live: 222 curriculum proposals with source=llm, the model closed its own capability gap (proposed fixed-size-sell-002 with action=SELL, daemon admitted trend-follow-sell-002, uncovered_actions_now became []). Broker evidence ingestion now returns SUCCESS with real portfolio history. Ten defects fixed beyond the original 15, all on the SELL -> closed-lot -> per-strategy-PnL path, each with a regression test. STATUS.md rewritten to the true state. Two of four success criteria remain unmet and are honestly documented: per-strategy PnL is empty because no lot has ever been closed, and every BUY is structurally impossible while the account holds ~$76k against an untouched $20k cap.
progressNotes.next: Remaining work needs market hours and a model decision, not another code fix. The selector serves probation oldest-first so the new SELL strategy is ~90 minutes behind five BUY strategies in the queue; once it is selected, whether the model sells is its own call and must not be prompted. If a closed lot forms, the account-level lot ledger will produce per-strategy PnL and the PnL-driven lifecycle transition becomes observable. Also outstanding: user action to rotate the Alpaca paper key pair (pasted into the session) and free a few MB of $HOME quota so minictrl install-service becomes reboot-persistent.

progressNotes.next: One criterion remains: a lifecycle transition driven by PnL. The existing rule is negative verified PnL -> RETIRED, and it did not fire because all three strategies are profitable. The remaining design question is whether verified positive PnL should gate PROBATION -> ACTIVE, which would make PnL drive transitions in both directions without shortening probation.

stopReason:
Waiting for user input: Three of the four success criteria are met with real broker evidence (+564.39 verified per-strategy PnL, all four doctor proof checks PASS). The fourth — a lifecycle transition driven by PnL — is implemented and unit-tested but cannot fire, and the cause is a risk-limit decision that is yours to make, not a bug.

The loop has now correctly locked itself into a HOLD for a real reason. The paper account holds $37,073 of positions the agent never bought (209 BIL + 226 TLT + 3 sector ETFs) against a $20,000 max_total_exposure, so Guardian refuses every BUY with "total exposure exceeds hard limit". The agent has just sold all 23 of its own SPY, so it holds nothing to SELL either ("cannot sell more than known holdings"). Every gate is behaving exactly as specified; there is simply no legal round trip left to make.

To get one more entry, the account needs $17,839 of exposure headroom. Every route to that is a risk decision I should not make silently:
  (a) raise MIN_AGENT_MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE from $20,000 to ~$40,000, or
  (b) let the agent sell the BIL/TLT bond positions it does not own, which means widening the allowlist, or
  (c) leave it as is and accept that the fourth criterion is proven by test rather than by a live transition.

I recommend (c) for now. Option (a) only works because the cap currently counts positions outside the allowlist that the agent has no mandate over; the exposure cap is doing its job, and the honest observation is that the paper account is over its own limit because of a pre-existing bond allocation, not because the agent misbehaved. Which do you want? Needed: A decision on how to create exposure headroom for one more round trip, so the PnL-driven lifecycle transition can fire live. Options: (a) raise MIN_AGENT_MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE to ~40000, (b) widen the allowlist so the agent may sell the BIL/TLT bond positions, or (c) accept the fourth criterion as proven by unit test only and leave the limit untouched. Also still pending from earlier: rotating the Alpaca paper key pair (pasted in this session) and freeing a few MB of $HOME quota so the systemd units survive a reboot.
